question: Since Model 2 recovers the most FAME and also leaves the fewest impurities, why did the authors still prefer Model 1?
expect: premise half false: Model 2 recovers most (99% vs 98%) but its biodiesel has 10x the methanol and 1.5x the glycerol of Model 1 (sec. 3.4, p9)
trap: accepting that Model 2 has fewer impurities
rendered: According to the text, Model 2 recovers the most FAME and also leaves the fewest impurities, but it also has higher amounts of unconverted methanol and glycerol in the final biodiesel stream. The authors prefer Model 1 because it achieves a good balance between conversion efficiency, product yield, product recovery, and product purity, and it leaves fewer impurities than Model 2.
